narrative:
The model determined that you have a 53% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three pieces of information about you. The single most important factor was that you plan to attend law school part-time. Among students who were admitted, only 7% planned to study part-time; the vast majority attended full-time. This choice strongly pushed the prediction toward failure.

Your first-year grades in law school were the second most important factor. You ranked in the 8th decile, noticeably higher than the average of accepted students (6th decile). This stronger academic performance worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing.

Your third-year grades were the third most influential piece of information. Ranking in the 6th decile, slightly above the accepted-student average, this also nudged the outcome slightly toward success, but not enough to overcome the part-time plan.

In short, although your grades are solid, the model saw the part-time schedule as a substantial risk for first-time bar passage. To improve your chances, consider reapplying with a full-time commitment or strengthening other parts of your profile that directly relate to bar-exam readiness, such as a higher LSAT score. This would give the model clearer signals of success. (218 words)
